transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I... I suppose I'm here because things at work have become incredibly difficult lately, and it's not because of the market or our quarterly projections, which are actually quite stable, all things considered. It's... it's the voices. I know how that sounds, but I keep hearing people talking about me. And it's not just a vague mumbling, it's incredibly specific. It usually happens when I'm in my office, and I can hear them through the conference room walls, even when I know for a fact the room is empty because my assistant just checked it. Or, and this is the part that really disrupts my day, I'll hear them coming from my phone. Not a call, mind you, but when the screen is completely black, completely turned off. 

It's usually the board members, or sometimes senior staff, and they're just... they're saying the most awful things. They're constantly saying that I'm ruining the company, that every decision I make is a disaster, that I'm incompetent. And the thing is, Doctor, it sounds so incredibly real. It's not like a thought in my head, it's an actual voice in the room. It's so clear that I've actually caught myself answering them out loud, defending my strategic decisions, before I look around and realize that I'm completely alone and no one else heard a thing. It's exhausting, frankly, trying to run a company when you're constantly having to argue with people who aren't even in the room.
Aside from feeling exhausted by this, how has your overall mood been lately?

Mood? Well, I... I haven't really stopped to think about my mood, to be perfectly honest with you. When you're managing a company of this size and overseeing as many moving parts as I do, you don't exactly have the luxury of sitting around taking inventory of your feelings every afternoon. You just have to push through the day and get things done. 

So, my mood... I mean, I'm not sad. I'm not sitting at my desk crying or feeling hopeless about the future of the business, nothing like that. As I said, our financials are actually quite strong right now. It's really just the constant, relentless interference from those voices that takes up all my mental bandwidth. I suppose if you were to ask my executive team, they might say I seem a bit more on edge or tense lately, but honestly, who wouldn't be? If you had the board of directors whispering cruel things through the speaker of your powered-off smartphone while you're trying to review a vendor contract, you wouldn't be focused on your mood either. You'd just be trying to survive the hour. 

So, no, I wouldn't say my mood is bad or down or anything. I just feel like a professional who is trying to do her job while dealing with this incredibly frustrating situation. It leaves very little room to even register a "mood," if I'm making any sense. I just wake up, check my emails, and brace myself for whatever they're going to start saying to me.
How long have you been hearing these voices?

Well, if I really sit down and trace it back... let me think. It was right around the end of the previous quarter. Yes, so that would make it about three months ago. I remember the timeline specifically because we were in the middle of preparing all the Q3 deliverables for the board, and I was working late most nights to ensure the margins looked exactly right before the presentation. 

I was sitting in my office, it must have been past 8 PM, and the executive floor was practically deserted. The cleaning staff had already done their rounds, so it was just me. And that's when I first noticed it coming through the conference room walls. At first, I just assumed one of the VPs had left a dial-in meeting running on the Polycom system, you know how people forget to disconnect the line? So I actually got up, walked down the hall, and went to check. The room was pitch black. The system was off. But I could still hear them talking about my leadership. 

And then, maybe a week after that, the issue with my phone started. So, yes, it's been a solid three months of this. Ninety days of just... relentless, unavoidable commentary. It's ironic, really, because in business, a quarter is the standard metric for evaluating performance, right? You measure everything in 90-day increments. And for this entire past quarter, for the last three months exactly, I've had to navigate this situation where they are just actively broadcasting their criticisms through the drywall and my completely powered-off smartphone. Three months of having to double-check if my screen is even lit up before I realize they're doing it again. It's just been a very long three months, Doctor.

Drugs? Oh, no, absolutely not. I mean, I can't even begin to imagine how someone in my position would even have the time or the inclination for something like that. My days are scheduled down to the quarter-hour, from the moment my alarm goes off at 5:30 AM until I finally shut my laptop at night. There's just no room in my life for recreational anything, let alone drugs. 

I suppose... well, I do drink coffee, obviously. I don't know if you count caffeine, but I probably have three, maybe four cups a day? Mostly just to keep my energy up during back-to-back meetings, especially when I have to review those dense financial reports that legal sends over. And occasionally, if we close a major deal or if there's a significant company milestone, I might have a single glass of wine at a dinner with the executive team. But even then, I never finish it. I always need to keep a clear head because you never know when an urgent email is going to come through or if there's going to be some sort of crisis I have to manage. 

But as for actual recreational drugs, marijuana, pills, whatever else people are doing these days... no. Never. I've never touched them. I've always believed that to lead effectively, you need absolute mental clarity. You need to be sharp. Which is exactly why this whole situation with the voices is so incredibly frustrating, because my mind is clear, I'm completely sober, I'm entirely focused on my work, and yet I still have to sit there and listen to them criticizing my every move through a phone that isn't even turned on. So, no, Doctor, no drugs. Just a very demanding job and this bizarre, exhausting situation.
Do you have any diagnosed medical conditions or physical health problems?

Medical conditions? No, no, nothing like that. I've always been remarkably healthy, actually. I mean, you have to be, don't you? When you're carrying the weight of an entire corporation on your shoulders, you can't afford to be calling in sick or taking weeks off for medical leave. The board wouldn't tolerate it, and frankly, I wouldn't tolerate it from myself. 

I actually had my annual executive physical—our firm requires it for all C-suite officers, it's a whole comprehensive workup they do over at the private clinic downtown—just about six months ago. They check everything. Blood panels, EKG, stress tests, the works. The physician there, Dr. Aris, he actually joked that I have the cardiovascular profile of someone ten years younger. He said my numbers were pristine. So, no diabetes, no high blood pressure, no thyroid issues... nothing. 

I don't even get seasonal colds, to be honest. I think when you operate at this level of adrenaline and responsibility, your immune system just sort of falls in line. You simply don't have the time to be unwell. I take my daily vitamins, I stay hydrated, I try to get a decent amount of sleep when the deliverables allow for it. But no, there are no underlying physical health problems whatsoever. My body is functioning perfectly. It's just... it's just this external interference, this constant barrage of criticism coming through the walls and the electronics. If it weren't for that, I'd be operating at 100 percent capacity. So physically, medically? I'm completely fine. Perfect bill of health.

Yes, almost exactly two years and four months. It coincides perfectly with the major company expansion we did back then. We had this massive corporate restructuring, and the board put me directly in charge of launching and overseeing the new arts-and-commerce division. Which, let me tell you, was just a colossal undertaking. You're trying to merge highly sensitive creative assets with hard commercial deliverables, and the logistics alone were an absolute nightmare. So yes, two years and four months of this building up behind the scenes.
